QUESTION:
In which release did the default of `auth.interval_s` change, and what was it before?

DOCUMENTATION EXCERPTS:
[d0697] config | auth.interval_s | version 4.x
# `auth.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `300` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | auth |
| Unit | s |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## Notes

Changes to `auth.interval_s` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[auth]
interval_s = 300
```

---

[d0895] config | auth.interval_s (PaderQueue 2.x) | version 2.x
# `auth.interval_s` (PaderQueue 2.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 2.x.

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `10` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | auth |
| Unit | s |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `auth.interval_s` only if you observe problems with the authentication module that validates client tokens, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[auth]
interval_s = 10
```
